claims.text: Multiphase refractory or eutectic high-entropy alloys can contain precipitate-bearing multiphase microstructures, including B2 or gamma-double-prime-related phases.
These alloys will exhibit a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during isothermal aging.
The initial alloy is ductile because its matrix is disordered and precipitates are absent.
Nucleation and growth of coherent ordered precipitates initially embrittle the alloy by creating strong dislocation barriers, brittle interfaces, or interfacial stress concentrations.
Precipitate growth or relaxation of interface coherency subsequently permits precipitate shearing or Orowan bypass and thereby restores ductility.
A reduction in brittle secondary phases during continued aging helps restore ductility.
Activation of multiple deformation mechanisms during continued treatment helps restore ductility.
The relevant initial state is an as-cast or solution-treated multiphase alloy with a disordered matrix, possible solute clusters or small ordered precipitates, and micrometer-scale grains.
Aging between approximately 0.5 Tm and 0.7 Tm, or about 600-800 degrees Celsius, for 1-1000 hours induces precipitation and chemical ordering.
The relevant mechanical-testing strain-rate range is 10^-4 to 10^-3 s^-1, with aging conducted in argon to prevent oxidation.
The structural mediator is the evolution of B2, L12, or D0a chemical ordering together with precipitate size distribution and coherent-to-semi-coherent-to-incoherent interface evolution.
Elongation to failure will exceed 15% initially, fall below 5% after approximately 10-50 hours, and recover above 15% after more than 200 hours.
Ultimate tensile strength will increase monotonically or reach a plateau with aging.
Standard multiphase AlCoCrFeNi- or NbTaTiV-type high-entropy alloys typically show monotonic strengthening and monotonic ductility loss during aging.
The proposed transition requires coherent or semi-coherent ordered precipitates and a matrix that remains ductile.
The transition may be absent when brittle sigma-like precipitates form or when ordering, such as B2 ordering, makes the matrix itself brittle.
The aging temperature must permit diffusion while avoiding complete coarsening or decomposition into non-coherent phases.
The timing of the brittle-to-ductile recovery depends on alloy composition and diffusion coefficients.
Initial grain size and residual stress may affect the magnitude of the ductility minimum.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes initial ductility to a lack of precipitates, whereas the initial-state field permits pre-existing ordered precipitates or solute clusters.
